"'''Go Away Little Girl'''" is a popular song written by [[Gerry Goffin]] and [[Carole King]]. It was first recorded by [[Bobby Vee]] for Liberty Records on March 28, 1962. The lyrics consist of a young man asking a young attractive woman to stay away from him, so that he will not be tempted to betray his steady girlfriend by kissing her. The song is notable for making the American Top 20 three times: for [[Steve Lawrence]] in 1963 (US number 1), for [[The Happenings]] in 1966 (US number 12; CAN number 10<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/obj/028020/f2/nlc008388.5775.pdf| title=RPM Top 100 Singles - November 14, 1966}}</ref>), and for [[Donny Osmond]] in 1971 (US number 1). It is also the first song, and [[List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones#Songs hitting number one for different artists|one of only nine, to reach US number 1 by two different artists]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/specials/hot100/charts/cover-me.shtml|title=Cover Me: Same Songs to Hit No. 1 By Two Different Artists|publisher=Billboard|access-date=10 February 2010}}</ref> Also notable in each of the solo versions is the similar [[double-tracked]] treatment of the singer's voice.

"Go Away Little Girl" is a popular song written by Gerry Goffin and Carole King. It was first recorded by Bobby Vee for Liberty Records on March 28, 1962. The lyrics consist of a young man asking a young attractive woman to stay away from him, so that he will not be tempted to betray his steady girlfriend by kissing her. The song is notable for making the American Top 20 three times: for Steve Lawrence in 1963 (US number 1), for The Happenings in 1966 (US number 12; CAN number 10), and for Donny Osmond in 1971 (US number 1). It is also the first song, and one of only nine, to reach US number 1 by two different artists. Also notable in each of the solo versions is the similar double-tracked treatment of the singer's voice.

sections.heading: Steve Lawrence version
sections.wikitext:
In late 1962, Steve Lawrence released the second recording of this song (Bobby Vee recorded it first in March 1962). The single reached number 1 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in January 1963 and remained in the top position for two weeks. This recording also spent six weeks atop the U.S. [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|Easy Listening]] chart.<ref>{{cite book |title= Top Adult Contemporary: 1961-2001|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2002 |publisher=Record Research |page=141}}</ref>   "Go Away Little Girl" went to number 14 on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot R&B Singles]] chart.<ref>{{cite book |title= Top R&B/Hip-Hop Singles: 1942-2004|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=343}}</ref> 
Outside the US, "Go Away Little Girl" also went to number 1 on the New Zealand Lever chart and number 18 in Canada.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://chumtribute.com/62-1-10-chart.jpg| title=CHUM Hit Parade - December 10, 1962}}</ref>
sections.text:
In late 1962, Steve Lawrence released the second recording of this song (Bobby Vee recorded it first in March 1962). The single reached number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in January 1963 and remained in the top position for two weeks. This recording also spent six weeks atop the U.S. Easy Listening chart.   "Go Away Little Girl" went to number 14 on the Hot R&B Singles chart. 
Outside the US, "Go Away Little Girl" also went to number 1 on the New Zealand Lever chart and number 18 in Canada.

Donny Osmond's [[cover version]] of "Go Away Little Girl" reached number 1 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart on September 11, 1971. It remained in the top position for three weeks. Osmond's version also went to number 36 on the Australian Go-Set chart.  It was certified Gold by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]] on October 13, 1971. Osmond was 13 at the time the song was recorded.

sections.heading: Certifications
Marlena Shaw version
sections.wikitext: [[Marlena Shaw]] does a version called "Yu-Ma/Go Away Little Boy" from her 1977 album ''Sweet Beginnings''. This reached number 21 on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' R&B chart staying in the Top 100 for 11 weeks.<ref>Joel Whitburn, Top R&B/Hip-Hop Singles, 1942-2004, Billboard, 2005</ref> In the 1980s it became a popular UK record on the [[Rare Groove]] dance scene. Ms. Shaw also performed a 9:31 live version of her "Go Away Little Boy" recorded for her ''It Is Love'' album.
sections.text: Marlena Shaw does a version called "Yu-Ma/Go Away Little Boy" from her 1977 album Sweet Beginnings. This reached number 21 on the Billboard R&B chart staying in the Top 100 for 11 weeks. In the 1980s it became a popular UK record on the Rare Groove dance scene. Ms. Shaw also performed a 9:31 live version of her "Go Away Little Boy" recorded for her It Is Love album.
